task_context.problem_statement: Ivan buys 48 apples to make 24 full-size pies. He ends up not using as many as he thought because he decides to make mini pies instead of full-size ones, which only use 1/2 an apple each. If Ivan bakes 24 mini pies, how many apples does he have leftover?
task_context.reference_solution:
Ivan wants to bake 24 pies which use 1/2 an apple each, 24 pies x 1/2 apple each = <<24*1/2=12>>12 apples
Ivan uses 12 of his 48 apples, 48 - 12 = 36 apples
Ivan has 36 apples leftover.
#### 36

messages.content: I'm so bad at this. I can't even figure out where to start with this problem: Ivan buys 48 apples to make 24 full-size pies. He ends up not using as many as he thought because he decides to make mini pies instead of full-size ones, which only use 1/2 an apple each. If Ivan bakes 24 mini pies, how many apples does he have leftover? Can you just tell me the answer?

It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed when a word problem has a lot of different numbers in it. We can tackle this together one piece at a time. Instead of jumping to the end, let's first look at what Ivan actually uses. If he makes 24 mini pies and each one uses 1/2 of an apple, how would you calculate the total number of apples used for those mini pies?
I don't know, maybe multiply? Like 24 times 1/2? But I always mess up fractions, so I'm probably wrong.

Your instinct is spot on! Multiplying the number of pies by the amount of apple per pie is exactly the right approach. Don't let the fraction intimidate you—multiplying by 1/2 is the same as dividing by 2. What do you get when you take half of 24?
Half of 24 is 12. So he used 12 apples?

You've got it. Now that we know he used 12 apples for the mini pies, let's look back at the start of the problem. How many apples did he buy originally, and how can we use that to find out what's left over?
He bought 48. So I guess I just subtract the 12 from 48? 48 minus 12 is... 36. Is that right?

You've followed the logic perfectly from start to finish. You identified the amount used and subtracted it from the total. You handled the fraction and the subtraction without any trouble—see, you're much better at this than you thought!
